attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The Cerro de los Siete Colores rising above the adobe village of Purmamarca in the Quebrada de Humahuaca
caption: The Cerro de los Siete Colores above Purmamarca, the first stop in the Quebrada de Humahuaca at about 2,200 m. A short loop track at its foot is the usual dawn walk, before the carnival crowds arrive.

attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Serranía de Hornocal, near Humahuaca, Jujuy
alt: The striped ridges of the Serranía de Hornocal seen from the viewpoint above Humahuaca
caption: The banded ridges of the Serranía de Hornocal, the '14 colours' hill, about 25 km of gravel road from Humahuaca. The viewpoint is near 4,350 m, so the group arrives acclimatised after nights at 2,200-3,000 m.

attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The white salt pan of the Salinas Grandes under a high-altitude sky
caption: The Salinas Grandes, a white salt pan at roughly 3,450 m reached by the Cuesta de Lipán from Purmamarca. Local Kolla communities run the salt-cutting stops, and the lithium debate here is part of the story.

attribution: Lifesan — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Red sandstone formations in the Quebrada de las Conchas beside Route 68
caption: Red sandstone formations in the Quebrada de las Conchas, the paved RN68 gorge between Cafayate and Salta. It is the last scenic day of the loop and a classic rainy-season washout risk.

attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Giant cardon cacti on the plateau of Los Cardones National Park
caption: Candelabra cardon cacti on the plateau of Los Cardones National Park, crossed on the way from Salta to Cachi. The road is gravel for the final stretch to Cachi.

commonsFile: File:La cuesta del Obispo, Ruta Provincial 33.jpg
attribution: Bachelot Pierre J-P — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Cuesta del Obispo, Ruta Provincial 33, Salta
alt: The winding gravel road of the Cuesta del Obispo climbing towards the Piedra del Molino pass
caption: The Cuesta del Obispo on provincial road 33, a switchback climb to the Piedra del Molino pass (about 3,348 m) that links the Lerma valley to the Calchaquí valleys. It is the gateway to Cachi and the least forgiving road of the trip in rain.

attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Reconstructed stone walls of the Pucará de Tilcara fortified settlement on its hill above the valley
caption: The reconstructed Pucará de Tilcara, a pre-Hispanic fortified settlement on a spur above the Río Grande. It sets the archaeological context before the group sees the carnival that is its living descendant.

commonsFile: File:Bajada de diablos del carnaval en Maimara - Jujuy. Argentina 12.jpg
attribution: Fede Tolay — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Dancers in devil costumes during the Bajada de diablos of the carnival in Maimará
caption: Costumed diablos during the carnival at Maimará, a village between Purmamarca and Tilcara. The unearthing of the pujllay doll, the devil figures and the offerings to the Pachamama are the cultural heart of this route in February.

attribution: Manuela Abuela — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The mountainside village of Iruya with its stone houses and church
caption: Iruya, a village of stone houses on a mountainside at about 2,780 m, reached by 50 km of unpaved road from the Quebrada. It is the most weather-dependent stop of the plan and the one with a built-in buffer day.

attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A whitewashed street in the colonial town of Cachi in the Calchaquí valleys
caption: A street in Cachi, a whitewashed Calchaquí valley town at about 2,280 m with a municipal campsite. It is the first night camped after the Quebrada and the start of the RN40 stage to Cafayate.

commonsFile: File:Salinas Grandes (Salta y Jujuy) - souvenir shops.jpg
attribution: Skimel — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Souvenir stalls built from salt blocks at the roadside of the Salinas Grandes
caption: Roadside stalls at the Salinas Grandes, where community members sell salt crafts and food. Buying from them directly is the simplest way to support the people who live and work on the pan.

attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Layered ochre, pink and green strata of the Serranía de Hornocal
caption: Close view of the layered strata of the Serranía de Hornocal. The ridge reaches about 4,760 m, so the group plans a slow ascent and a late-afternoon visit with water and warm layers.
